function: Reason function: KAN and DSR discover closed-form large-scale path-loss formulas (propagation modeling for network planning), not a function of the seven areas (p. 1, p. 4, p. 15).
notes: Excluded with code function (Step 1, item 5). The learned methods, Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (pykan) and Deep Symbolic Regression (an RNN trained by policy gradients), regress large-scale path loss in dB on distance, frequency, wall/floor counts and antenna height to discover interpretable path-loss formulas. p. 1: "this paper proposes a novel approach that accelerates the discovery of pathloss (PL) models"; p. 4: "we aim to automatically learn the most likely expression, i.e., formulas, that best describe the respective PL"; p. 15: "can be integrated into system-level analysis and planning tools". Training and test data are synthetic ABG/CI path-loss samples (p. 6: "The dataset consists of 1,000 instances.") and LoRaWAN indoor/outdoor measurements (p. 4: "derived empirical PL models for LoRaWAN"). No learned component estimates, compresses, feeds back, predicts, or synthesizes the channel state of a communication link, and there is no detection, beamforming, RIS configuration, OTFS, ISAC, NTN control, or over-the-air aggregation; RIS and mMIMO appear only as motivation in the abstract (p. 1). Codes 1 to 4 do not apply: it is a research article that proposes and evaluates a learned method, and the learning models a propagation quantity rather than a network decision, although the formulas are meant for network planning (p. 2, p. 16). For the reviewer: if learned path-loss prediction were read as channel prediction or synthesis of area 2, the work would still be excluded, with code system, since the paper models no multi-antenna or RIS link (LoRaWAN measurements and scalar ABG/CI path-loss values). The PDF is the published version, and its first page holds the title "Automated Modeling Method for Pathloss Model Discovery" and DOI 10.1109/TMC.2026.3683609.
